content.text:
I reviewed the brief line by line against the 8-K exhibit. Summary of findings:

**Key facts:** 8 of 10 are stated correctly. Two are absent: commercial remaining performance obligation (+84% to $678 billion) and the quarterly capex figure (additions to property and equipment of $35,802 million vs. $17,079 million a year earlier) — a notable omission given the balance sheet section the brief does include.

**Two problems in the claims:**
1. *Total assets* — the brief says $758.3 billion; the balance sheet shows $758,376 million, which rounds to $758.4 billion. Truncation, not rounding.
2. *OpenAI impact basis error* — the brief says the $480 million net income / $0.07 EPS increase was "on a non-GAAP basis." It is the opposite: those amounts are the OpenAI gains embedded in the **GAAP** results, which are *removed* to arrive at the non-GAAP figures. That is why non-GAAP net income ($35,286M) is *lower* than GAAP ($35,766M). This is the kind of error that inverts the read on earnings quality, so it should be corrected before the brief circulates.

Everything else — revenue, operating income, both EPS bases, full-year revenue, all three segments, Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, the $10.2 billion of capital returned, cash and investments, the guidance statement, and the $3.2 billion Anthropic gain driving the $0.27 benefit versus the April 29 guidance — checks out.

facts.evidence: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, was $90.0 billion, an increase of 18% (17% in constant currency) compared to the same period last year.
Diluted earnings per share were $4.81 on a GAAP basis (up 32%)
Diluted earnings per share were ... $4.74 on a non-GAAP basis (up 23%).
Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 43%.
Operating income was $40.6 billion, an increase of 18% over the prior year.
Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $59.3 billion, up 27% year-over-year

The committee should note the $3.2 billion gain from the investment in Anthropic and lower-than-expected expenses related to the Voluntary Retirement Program, which contributed to a $0.27 benefit on diluted earnings per share compared to prior guidance.
More Personal Computing revenue was $12.9 billion, a decrease of 4% (down 5% in constant currency).
